newsitem.title: USA: Explorer shuts southern line for planned repairs.
newsitem.headline: Explorer shuts southern line for planned repairs.

text.p: The Explorer Pipeline on Monday morning shut down the southern part of its refined oil products pipeline for one day of planned maintenance unrelated to cold weather, according to a company source.
The line, which carries over a half million barrels of distillates and gasoline a day from the Gulf Coast to the Midwest, has origin points in Pasadena, Texas, and in Lake Charles, Louisiana.
A segment of the line was shut down between Pasadena and the northern Texas town of Durand, temporarily halting shipments from the Gulf to Tulsa, Oklahoma, the source said.
"But everything should flow normal from Tulsa to points north" on Monday, he added, noting that the pipeline is fed in Oklahoma by tank farms located in the product-rich state.
"We will be down all day in the southern part of the line but should be up and running back to normal Tuesday," he added.
Another company official said Explorer conducts repairs like today's about once every two weeks througout the year as part of a plan to replace valves along its route.
Although Texas experienced freezing temperatures early Monday and Tulsa saw the mercury drop to 10 degrees Fahrenheit, Explorer said the pipeline was unaffected by the cold weather.
((- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1632))
